fields.question: Why exchange Wukong and HSTU state bidirectionally at every layer rather than only at the end?
fields.answer: Field interactions model high-order combinations and sequences capture evolving behavior. Cross-attention lets each guide later processing by the other. This adds dependencies and cost, not reusable user-only caching; local evidence is scaled public evaluation.
fields.example: Weekend context can focus sequence attention on camping, then updated interests inform price/category interactions.

fields.question: Why keep linear and deep paths together?
fields.answer: Wide memorizes sparse observed crosses; deep embeddings generalize to unseen combinations. One jointly trained logit combines them, rather than alternating independent services.
fields.example: Memorize frequent combinations and generalize related new ones.

fields.question: How can wide memorization and deep generalization each fail?
fields.answer: Memorization misses unseen crosses, while similarity can overgeneralize to incompatible combinations. Capacity should match sparsity and feature engineering.
fields.example: Semantic similarity does not establish accessory compatibility.

fields.question: Does local Wide & Deep use production Google Play crosses?
fields.answer: No. MovieLens replaces private logs and distributed training/serving. Add logits before sigmoid and train jointly, rather than averaging post-sigmoid probabilities.
fields.example: sigmoid(a+b) generally differs from averaging sigmoid(a) and sigmoid(b).

fields.question: Why train crosses and deep features jointly rather than average independent scores?
fields.answer: Both contribute one logit and share objective gradients, allowing complementary learning. Handcrafted crosses have limited coverage and deep generalization can be wrong.
fields.example: Wide memorizes a frequent user–category cross while deep transfers to related new combinations.

fields.question: Why generate X-Rec triggers on the item embedding sphere?
fields.answer: Normalized continuous vectors query multiple regions directly without SID quantization or token-by-token decoding. Anchors condition flow toward valid item neighborhoods.
fields.example: Generate different interest directions and retrieve nearby catalog items.

fields.question: How does spherical flow differ from Euclidean interpolation?
fields.answer: Geodesic paths and tangent projection preserve normalization. Straight lines can leave the sphere. Reusing earlier history layers is a separate efficiency design.
fields.example: The midpoint of two unit vectors is generally not unit length.

fields.question: Does local X-Rec have a GPU throughput receipt, and what runs?
fields.answer: No. CPU runs scaled anchors, geodesic RFM, final-layer KV reuse, and spherical Euler. No industrial ANN, streaming, or online A/B; CPU timings are not production throughput.
fields.example: Caching history verifies skipped computation without proving A100 gains.

fields.question: Why condition flow on normalized item space instead of generating SID tokens?
fields.answer: Continuous triggers avoid code quantization and use ANN directly. Coarse anchors condition geodesic noise-to-item flow; tangent projection preserves geometry. Cache earlier history layers and denoise final-layer tokens. Multistep cost remains and local low-budget outcomes are negative.
fields.example: Generate camera/lens directions around a photography anchor rather than decoding integer IDs.

fields.question: Why use a deep user tower for YouTube candidate generation?
fields.answer: Combine heterogeneous history and context embeddings into a user vector, train next-watch classification, and retrieve neighbors. Fine ranking is separate.
fields.example: Narrow millions of videos before applying richer ranking features.

fields.question: What does a deep user tower add over matrix factorization?
fields.answer: It dynamically combines history/context instead of looking up fixed user/item factors. One vector can still compress away distinct interests.
fields.example: Recent preference shifts can enter the tower without retraining a user ID vector.

fields.question: How align next-watch softmax training and serving retrieval?
fields.answer: Use the same score space and item-vector version with time-causal history. Do not mix sampled training probabilities and full-catalog metrics. The public implementation lacks the original inventory and stack.
fields.example: Refresh the item index after user-space changes.

fields.question: Why train next watch as classification but serve nearest neighbors?
fields.answer: A nonlinear user tower and item dot products define training logits. The same dot-product space supports indexing candidates, avoiding a complex per-video forward. Recall scores are not final ranking utility.
fields.example: Compute one user vector, retrieve from a million-item index, and then apply fine ranking.

fields.question: Why separate training debiasing from serving exploration for freshness?
fields.answer: Historical exposure favors old items. IPS/bias towers change learning signals, while uncertainty exploration changes actual exposures. Age features alone do not fix feedback loops.
fields.example: Old songs have more data because they were shown; new songs need actual opportunities.

fields.question: How does a removable bias tower differ from retaining recency in serving?
fields.answer: A tower can absorb training exposure bias then be removed. Recency remains a serving signal. Do not keep adding learned exposure bias as quality.
fields.example: Learning old items' logging advantage need not reward them again in deployment.

fields.question: Do local SNGP proxies or negative results explain YouTube's live study?
fields.answer: No. There is no full SNGP or continual training. Report interventions, logging propensities, and budgets separately. Popularity is not a measured IPS propensity.
fields.example: Low popularity does not establish a low historical impression probability.

fields.question: Why separate debiasing and exploration instead of relying on freshness features?
fields.answer: Content age does not fix logged exposure selection. IPS and removable bias towers adjust training; SNGP uncertainty gives unknown items exposure online. Both depend on assumptions, and less head concentration does not prove satisfaction.
fields.example: A new video may lack clicks because it has never been shown; explore and collect feedback rather than boosting all new videos blindly.

fields.question: Why fuse many features into a few Prime Tokens?
fields.answer: Fewer wider tokens reduce interaction count and retain capacity; differentiated attention and independent enhancement counter homogenization. Compression can still lose detail.
fields.example: Put sparse fields in several wide slots without making every slot identical.

fields.question: How does token-specific TSwiGLU differ from shared FFNs?
fields.answer: Independent transformations let roles specialize, but add parameters. Match budgets before attributing gains to architecture.
fields.example: User and item slots may benefit from different nonlinearities.

fields.question: Does local Zenith establish a scaling law?
fields.answer: No. Small fixed data exercises fusion, differentiated interaction, and enhancement without production hardware or size. A scaling slope needs matched multi-size curves.
fields.example: A win at one scale does not imply the gap grows with size.

fields.question: Why compress heterogeneous features into wide Prime Tokens and then enhance each separately?
fields.answer: Token Fusion trades fewer positions for wider channels; RSA/TMHSA maintain differentiation and SwiGLU or MoE adds role-specific transformations. Check information loss and matched compute.
fields.example: Reduce pairwise interactions over 100 fields while preserving meaningful user/item roles.

fields.question: Does zero training mean ZoRRO needs no representation model?
fields.answer: No. It uses existing article embeddings and categories, with fixed temporal/semantic rules instead of fitting ranker parameters. Existing models and hyperparameters still cost resources.
fields.example: Retrieve with external vectors without backpropagating on news logs.

fields.question: How does time-decayed semantic scoring differ from popularity?
fields.answer: It changes by individual history and age, while popularity mostly shares global trends. Category adds structure; semantic similarity can still cause repetition and miss freshness.
fields.example: Two readers can rank the same articles differently.

fields.question: Does a movie proxy establish high-throughput online news behavior?
fields.answer: No. MovieLens lacks news timeliness, private traffic, and serving. Fix age, cutoff, category source, and weights; do not tune per test case and claim zero-training generalization.
fields.example: Movie age is only a mechanism proxy for fresh news.

fields.question: Why can ZoRRO rank without training, and what limits it?
fields.answer: Combine history recency, semantic similarity, and category in fixed rules. New history updates scores immediately without fitting, but cannot learn complex collaborative and user-specific relations. Features, data, and hyperparameters still matter.
fields.example: Recent technology reading raises related articles without learning that one user prefers culture on weekends.
